assessment: The authors tested the hypothesis that individual hummingbirds employ torpor as an energy-saving mechanism to facilitate migratory fattening, even when starvation is not imminent. This is a difficult hypothesis to test because of the difficulties associated with repeatedly and accurately measuring body composition in individual migratory birds. Using captive experiments, the authors provide some indication that hummingbirds use torpor during energy emergencies in the summer – rare empirical evidence supporting the hypothesis that hummingbirds use torpor to facilitate migratory fitting.
